pages.d: Practical operator training: safety, mission planning, equipment maintenance and first working day preparation.
pages.x: Practical operator training: safety, mission planning, equipment maintenance and first working day preparation. At PDG Academy operators learn in the field, on real equipment: pre-flight checks, mission planning, battery and charging routine, spray system care and how to organise the first working day.

pages.d: The number of batteries, the charging setup and their care decide how much the drone can work in a day.
pages.x: Guide The number of batteries, the charging setup and their care decide how much the drone can work in a day. How many batteries you need The drone flies while the next battery charges. Flight time and charging time have to match, so larger areas need more batteries and chargers. We will choose the right number for your area and working day together. Power in the field There is not always mains power in the field. A generator and a parallel charging kit let you charge where you work. Use the equipment the manufacturer recommends. Cooling and temperature On a hot day a battery warms up in flight. Cool it before charging, for example with a cooling tower. Charging a hot battery shortens its life. Storage between seasons After the season, store batteries in a dry, cool place at the charge level the manufacturer specifies. Do not use a damaged or swollen battery.

pages.t: How to choose an agricultural drone
pages.d: Start with the work you need to do. Then choose the equipment.
pages.x: Guide Start with the work you need to do. Then choose the equipment. Your fields and crops Assess the area, field shape, terrain and access roads. Open fields, vineyards and orchards need different planning. Workload is about more than hectares alone. The complete workflow Plan charging, water supply, transport and staffing alongside the drone. The number of batteries and chargers should match your actual working schedule. Service and parts Before buying, establish how you will receive technical support, which parts are available and what the training covers. Compare the cost of the complete package and its operation. A practical demonstration Describe your crops, acreage and tasks during the consultation. Request an offer suited to your conditions and verify the drone's capabilities in the manufacturer's documentation.

pages.d: Training, technical checks and planning your work.
pages.x: In practice Training, technical checks and planning your work. Know your equipment Complete practical training for your model and read the manufacturer's manual. Learn the operating modes, warnings and procedures for stopping a flight before you begin. Check the drone Follow the manufacturer's checklist to inspect the frame, propellers, batteries and spraying system. Do not start a flight with faulty equipment or unresolved warnings. Inspect the work site Identify obstacles, power lines and areas where people may be present. Assess the weather and whether the work fits the manufacturer's limits and applicable requirements. Plan the treatment Choose the product and application rate with an agronomist and according to the product label. During training, check operating parameters against the manufacturer's instructions. This guide does not replace practical training.

pages.d: In season, even one day of downtime is expensive. Service and parts close by keep that time short.
pages.x: In practice In season, even one day of downtime is expensive. Service and parts close by keep that time short. Pre-season check Before the season, check the motors, propellers, pumps, nozzles and cables. A small fault found early saves a long stop in the field. Original parts A non-original part can change how the drone works and how safe it is. Original XAG parts for the P150 MAX are in stock in our warehouse in Georgia. Regular care After every working day, rinse the spraying system and inspect the drone. Follow the manufacturer’s manual or ask our team about care routines. When something is not right If the drone shows a warning or behaves strangely, stop flying and contact us. We do the diagnostics and repairs ourselves.
